Ram.description: A revered Hindu deity, Lord Rama; uttering his name is considered auspicious at the time of death.

Rao Pavn.description: A person to whom Namdev communicates about Shyam's letter; possibly an acquaintance or family friend.

Tukaram.description: Another of Shyam's brothers, mentioned as waiting for Shyam at home.

Durva's grandmother.description: An elderly woman in the village who tells stories to children, including the tale of Chindhi, and offers wisdom during rituals.

Bhatmama.description: Shyam's maternal uncle and village priest who supports the family during hardships and assists with funeral rituals.

Boribunder.description: A major railway station in Mumbai (now known as Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus), where Shyam disembarks.

Girgaon.description: A neighborhood in Mumbai, indicating Shyam's journey through the city.

Gitanjali.description: A collection of poems by Rabindranath Tagore, reflecting spiritual and emotional themes.

Harnai.description: A coastal port town in Maharashtra, where Shyam arrives by boat.

Gita.description: A reference to the Bhagavad Gita, a sacred Hindu scripture.

Geetanjali.description: Another spelling of 'Gitanjali', Tagore's collection of poems.

pindadaan.description: A Hindu ritual of offering rice balls (pinda) to departed souls to help them attain peace.

pind.description: A rice ball offered during Hindu funeral rites as part of pindadaan.

darbha grass.description: A type of sacred grass used in Hindu rituals, especially during funeral ceremonies.

Mathi.description: The family cat who was deeply attached to Shyam's mother and whose devotion is highlighted in this chapter.

Paingin.description: A village in Canacona, Goa, mentioned as the place of residence or origin in the library information.

Canacona.description: A region in the southern part of Goa, India.

Shri Shraddhanand Vidyalaya.description: A school in Goa where the author or a related person served as Headmaster.

Om Shri Datt Padmaja Prakashan.description: A publishing house based in Shristhal, Canacona, Goa.

Shristhal.description: A locality in Canacona, Goa, mentioned as the location of the publishing house.

Konkani.description: An Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in the state of Goa and surrounding regions.

ch-1-15: Shri Ram Jai Ram, Jai Jai Ram
